derivedFrom.revisedAgainstSpecs: The ledger classification was the starting point, not the authority. Every row was re-derived from the milestone spec, required experiments and validation matrix in docs/milestones.json and docs/milestones/*/VALIDATION.md, plus docs/VALIDATION-PLAN.md. Nine rows moved: M0-AC06 and M0-AC09 to config-experiment, M1-AC09 to installed, M2-AC12 and M6-AC09 to benchmark, M3-AC10 and M6-AC06 to accessory, M5-AC09 to gui, M6-AC11 to per-claim. The ledger is a dated account of one run and is not rewritten to match.

note: Two questions, not one. A surface answers where a pass can be obtained; runsPerPullRequest answers whether an ordinary pull request -- the one under review, on this repository, with no extra apparatus -- reaches that surface. Conflating them was wrong in both directions: criteria whose evidence is repository and CI inspection but which need purpose-built pull requests were counted as reachable, and criteria at level I whose prescribed measurement is a named local machine were counted as hosted CI. Two surfaces may therefore share a location and differ in reach: config and config-experiment are both repository and CI inspection. This file records where a criterion CAN be validated and nothing about whether it HAS been. That is docs/ACCEPTANCE-EVIDENCE.json, and a surface here is never evidence there.

automated.runsOn: Linux container and hosted macos-26 CI
automated.establishes: Pure functions, schemas, known fixtures, simulated faults, bit-exact encoding.
automated.doesNotEstablish: Native print dialog, installed scheduler behaviour or physical output.

config.runsOn: repository and CI inspection on the pull request under review
config.establishes: Actual repository settings, CI execution, action pins and policy inspection.
config.doesNotEstablish: Product behaviour not covered by executed tests, or CI behaviour that only a purpose-built pull request can show.

macos-native.establishes: Real Apple frameworks and executables on a recorded Apple Silicon runtime.
macos-native.doesNotEstablish: Application dialogs, an installed scheduler, a retail host, any device, a non-Apple-Silicon runtime, or a performance threshold: the plan treats shared hosted-runner timing as informational only.

config-experiment.runsOn: dedicated pull requests built for the experiment, including a contributor-like fork
config-experiment.establishes: CI behaviour that only a purpose-built pull request can show: an intentionally failing check blocking the aggregate, a documentation-only change not stranding required checks, and a fork pull request running the allowed checks without maintainer secrets.
config-experiment.doesNotEstablish: Anything an ordinary pull request shows about itself. The experiment branches are temporary and only the intentional failure is removed afterwards; the observations are recorded, not the branches.

gui.establishes: Required applications, the system print dialog, the extraction editor, accessibility.
gui.doesNotEstablish: Physical output. Earlier attempts failed with cgWindowNotFound; the surface is uncertified.

installed.runsOn: test Mac with an installed scheduler or helper
installed.establishes: Real CUPS queues, held jobs, ownership, the privileged boundary, install and uninstall lifecycle.
installed.doesNotEstablish: Physical output. Requires separate installation authorization.

benchmark.runsOn: the named reference Mac, release build, with a retained baseline commit
benchmark.establishes: Latency, peak memory, output bytes and throughput measured repeatably on one recorded machine with the same fixtures and media, which is what a reviewed threshold can be set against.
benchmark.doesNotEstablish: Anything from shared hosted-runner timing, which the plan and the M2 and M6 specs treat as informational and not a precise performance SLA. Not a physical or mechanical speed.

per-claim.runsOn: one session per advertised claim, in the environment that claim itself names
per-claim.establishes: Exactly the one advertised claim whose own evidence was obtained: an Intel claim by execution on Intel, an IPP claim by exercising its integration path, an extra transport by a session on that transport.
per-claim.doesNotEstablish: Any claim from compilation, from a hosted Apple Silicon run, or from another claim's evidence. There is no single session for this surface. An unexercised claim is withdrawn or marked unavailable, never carried; where a claim additionally needs device observation, that H evidence is recorded separately.

physical.establishes: Observed output, status and finishing on a named device configuration.
physical.doesNotEstablish: Other resolutions, firmware, accessories or the model family; the S1 unit is tear-off with no cutter, so no cut or peel behaviour can be observed on it. Needs explicit consent naming the device and a finite label budget.

accessory.runsOn: an approved accessory target: a printer that actually has the cutter or peeler under test
accessory.establishes: Observed cut policy per label, per batch and at end of job, and peel wait and resume behaviour, on hardware that has the accessory.
accessory.doesNotEstablish: Anything about the S1 tear-off GC420d, which has no cutter and disabled peel behaviour, and nothing the S1 baseline can supply. This is deferred S2 hardware; without it these behaviours stay explicitly unqualified and gate full parity closure.

release.establishes: Exact candidate installation and distribution lifecycle, declared signing mode and provenance.
release.doesNotEstablish: Untested configurations or all future releases. A clean user account is not a clean host.
